functions.source:
def save_checkpoint(prefix, params, cfg: ModelConfig, tok: Tokenizer):
    folder = os.path.dirname(prefix)
    if folder:
        os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)

    np.savez(prefix + ".npz", **params) # keys like "b0.wq" are kept as they are

    with open(prefix + ".json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(asdict(cfg), f)

    # stoi is not saved, it is just itos turned around, so load rebuilds it
    # json has no tuples, so each merge's "pair" is stored as a list, merge_tokens only
    # uses pair[0] and pair[1], so a list works exactly the same
    with open(prefix + ".tok.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump({"merges": tok.merges, "itos": tok.itos}, f, ensure_ascii=False)

functions.source:
def make_windows(ids, seq_len, stride = 1):
    if len(ids) <= seq_len:
        raise ValueError(f"need more than seq_len={seq_len} tokens, got {len(ids)}")
 
    starts = np.arange(0, len(ids) - seq_len, stride)
    rows = starts[:, None] + np.arange(seq_len)
 
    inputs = pd.DataFrame(ids[rows])
    targets = pd.DataFrame(ids[rows + 1])
    return inputs, targets

leadingComments: Training doesn’t use all windows at once, because that would make each update slow. It also doesn’t use one window at a time, because that would make updates noisy. This function hands out batch_size windows at a time.

functions.name: numerical_grad
functions.source:
def numerical_grad(f, x, h = 1e-5):
    g = np.zeros_like(x)
    for idx in np.ndindex(*x.shape):
        old = x[idx]
        x[idx] = old + h
        fp = f(x)
        x[idx] = old - h
        fm = f(x)
        x[idx] = old
        g[idx] = (fp - fm) / (2 * h)

    return g

def relative_error(a, b, eps = 1e-12):
    return abs(a - b) / max(abs(a), abs(b), eps)

functions.source:
def check_params(loss_fn, params, grads, rng, samples_per_param = 5, h = 1e-5):
    worst: dict[str, float] = {}
    for name, W in params.items():
        w = 0.0
        for _ in range(samples_per_param):
            idx = tuple(int(rng.integers(s)) for s in W.shape)
            old = W[idx]
            W[idx] = old + h
            fp = loss_fn(params)
            W[idx] = old - h
            fm = loss_fn(params)
            W[idx] = old
            w = max(w, relative_error(grads[name][idx], (fp - fm) / (2 * h)))
        worst[name] = w
    return worst

def linear_backward(X, W, dY):
    dW = X.T @ dY
    db = dY.sum(axis=0)
    dX = dY @ W.T
    return dX, dW, db

def cross_entropy_backward(probs, targets):
    T = len(targets)
    dZ = probs.copy()
    dZ[np.arange(T), targets] -= 1.0
    return dZ / T

def layer_norm_backward(dY, cache, gamma):
    Xhat, s = cache
    dXhat = dY * gamma
    dX = s * (dXhat - dXhat.mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
                - Xhat * (dXhat * Xhat).mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    
    dgamma = (dY * Xhat).sum(axis=0)
    dbeta = dY.sum(axis=0)
    return dX, dgamma, dbeta

def __init__(self, params, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-8, weight_decay=0.0):
        self.m = {k: np.zeros_like(v) for k, v in params.items()} # running average of the gradient (which direction to go)
        self.v = {k: np.zeros_like(v) for k, v in params.items()} # running average of gradient squared (how big the gradients usually are)
        self.t = 0 # step counter, needed for bias correction
        self.b1, self.b2, self.eps, self.wd = beta1, beta2, eps, weight_decay

methods.name: step
methods.source:
def step(self, params, grads, lr):
        self.t += 1 # first step is t=1, so 1 - b1**t is never zero

        for k in params:
            g = grads[k]

            self.m[k] = self.b1 * self.m[k] + (1 - self.b1) * g # mostly old direction, a little new gradient
            self.v[k] = self.b2 * self.v[k] + (1 - self.b2) * g * g # same idea, but for the squared gradient

            mhat = self.m[k] / (1 - self.b1 ** self.t) # m starts at 0 so it is too small early on, this scales it back up
            vhat = self.v[k] / (1 - self.b2 ** self.t)

            update = mhat / (np.sqrt(vhat) + self.eps) # direction divided by typical size, so every number moves about lr per step

            if params[k].ndim >= 2: # weight decay only for matrices, not biases or layer norm gamma/beta
                update = update + self.wd * params[k] # shrink the weight a little, outside the m/v part (this is the "W" in AdamW)

            params[k] -= lr * update # changes the array in place, nothing to return

class Adam:
    def __init__(self, params, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-8, weight_decay=0.0):
        self.m = {k: np.zeros_like(v) for k, v in params.items()} # running average of the gradient (which direction to go)
        self.v = {k: np.zeros_like(v) for k, v in params.items()} # running average of gradient squared (how big the gradients usually are)
        self.t = 0 # step counter, needed for bias correction
        self.b1, self.b2, self.eps, self.wd = beta1, beta2, eps, weight_decay

    def step(self, params, grads, lr):
        self.t += 1 # first step is t=1, so 1 - b1**t is never zero

        for k in params:
            g = grads[k]

            self.m[k] = self.b1 * self.m[k] + (1 - self.b1) * g # mostly old direction, a little new gradient
            self.v[k] = self.b2 * self.v[k] + (1 - self.b2) * g * g # same idea, but for the squared gradient

            mhat = self.m[k] / (1 - self.b1 ** self.t) # m starts at 0 so it is too small early on, this scales it back up
            vhat = self.v[k] / (1 - self.b2 ** self.t)

            update = mhat / (np.sqrt(vhat) + self.eps) # direction divided by typical size, so every number moves about lr per step

            if params[k].ndim >= 2: # weight decay only for matrices, not biases or layer norm gamma/beta
                update = update + self.wd * params[k] # shrink the weight a little, outside the m/v part (this is the "W" in AdamW)

            params[k] -= lr * update # changes the array in place, nothing to return

def test_tokenizer_round_trips(saved):
    prefix, _, _, tok = saved
    t2 = load_checkpoint(prefix)[2]
    assert t2.itos == tok.itos
    assert t2.stoi == tok.stoi
    assert t2.vocab_size == tok.vocab_size
    for s in ["low newest", "lower tower", "  low  ", "low!"]:   # "!" was never seen
        assert t2.encode(s) == tok.encode(s), s
        assert t2.decode(t2.encode(s)) == tok.decode(tok.encode(s)), s
    assert t2.encode("low!")[-1] == 0                # unseen character is still <unk>

def test_batches_cover_every_window_once():
    x, y = make_windows(np.arange(50), seq_len=4)         # 46 windows
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    seen, sizes = [], []
    for xb, yb in iterate_batches(x, y, batch_size=16, rng=rng):
        assert xb.shape == yb.shape and xb.shape[1] == 4
        assert (yb[:, :-1] == xb[:, 1:]).all()            # pairs stay aligned
        seen.extend(xb[:, 0].tolist())
        sizes.append(len(xb))
    assert sorted(seen) == list(range(46))
    assert sizes == [16, 16, 14]

def test_key_bias_gradient_is_zero():
    # adding the same vector to every key shifts each score row by a constant,
    # softmax ignores constants, so dL/dbk must be 0
    cfg, params, ids, targets, rng = tiny_setup()
    _, grads = loss_and_grads(params, ids, targets, cfg)
    for l in range(cfg.num_layers):
        assert np.abs(grads[f"b{l}.bk"]).max() < 1e-12

def test_linear_worked_example():
    X = np.array([[1., 2.], [0., 1.]])
    W = np.array([[1., 0., 2.], [-1., 1., 0.]])
    b = np.array([0., 1., -1.])
    dY = np.array([[1., 0., 1.], [0., 2., -1.]])
    assert np.allclose(linear_forward(X, W, b), [[-1, 3, 1], [-1, 2, -1]])
    dX, dW, db = linear_backward(X, W, dY)
    assert np.allclose(dW, [[1, 0, 1], [2, 2, 1]])
    assert np.allclose(db, [1, 2, 0])
    assert np.allclose(dX, [[3, -1], [-2, 2]])

def main(prefix="checkpoints/model"):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(config.seed)

    # 1. text -> ids -> train/val windows (split BEFORE windowing)
    text = load_corpus(config.corpus_path, config.corpus_column, config.max_rows)
    tok = build_tokenizer(text, config.num_merges)
    ids = encode_corpus(text, tok)
    train_ids, val_ids = split_ids(ids, config.val_fraction)
    tr_x, tr_y = make_windows(train_ids, config.seq_len, config.stride)
    va_x, va_y = make_windows(val_ids, config.seq_len, config.stride)

    # 2. model + optimiser
    cfg = ModelConfig(tok.vocab_size, config.context_len, config.emb_dim,
                      config.num_heads, config.ff_dim, config.num_layers)
    params = init_params(cfg, rng)
    opt = Adam(params, config.beta1, config.beta2, config.adam_eps, config.weight_decay)
    print(f"V={cfg.vocab_size}  ln V={math.log(cfg.vocab_size):.3f}")

    steps_per_epoch = math.ceil(len(tr_x) / config.batch_size)
    total_steps = config.epochs * steps_per_epoch

    # 3. the loop: gradient -> clip -> learning rate -> Adam
    step = 0
    for epoch in range(config.epochs):
        for xb, yb in iterate_batches(tr_x, tr_y, config.batch_size, rng):
            loss, grads = batch_loss_and_grads(params, xb, yb, cfg)
            norm = clip_grad_norm(grads, config.grad_clip)
            step += 1
            lr = lr_schedule(step, config.warmup_steps, total_steps,
                             config.lr_max, config.lr_min)
            opt.step(params, grads, lr)
            if step == 1 or step % 50 == 0:
                print(f"step {step:5d}  loss {loss:.3f}  |g| {norm:.2f}  lr {lr:.5f}")

        v = validation_loss(params, cfg, va_x, va_y)
        print(f"epoch {epoch + 1}: val loss {v:.3f}  ppl {perplexity(v):.1f}")
        seed_ids = [int(i) for i in va_x.iloc[0][:3]]
        out = generate(params, cfg, seed_ids, 30, config.seq_len,
                       config.temperature, config.top_k, config.top_p, rng)
        print("  sample:", repr(tok.decode(out)))

    # 4. keep the trained model so talk.py can load it later
    save_checkpoint(prefix, params, cfg, tok)
    print(f"saved checkpoint to {prefix}.*")

    return params, cfg, tok

functions.name: init_params
functions.source:
def init_params(cfg: ModelConfig, rng):
    d, F, V = cfg.emb_dim, cfg.ff_dim, cfg.vocab_size

    p = {
        "tok_emb": xavier_uniform(V, d, rng), # lookup table with one row per vocabulary token
        "pos_emb": xavier_uniform(cfg.context_len, d, rng) # second table with one row per position, weighted average of values
        # input to first block is tok_emb + pos_emb
        # this makes cat at first position and fifth position different in a sentence
    }

    for l in range(cfg.num_layers):
        b = f"b{l}." # key
        p[b + "ln1_g"], p[b + "ln1_b"] = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d) # layer norm

        for n in "qkvo":
            p[b + "w" + n] = xavier_uniform(d, d, rng)
            p[b + "b" + n] = np.zeros(d)

        p[b + "ln2_g"], p[b + "ln2_b"] = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d)
        p[b + "ff1_w"], p[b + "ff1_b"] = xavier_uniform(d, F, rng), np.zeros(F)
        p[b + "ff2_w"], p[b + "ff2_b"] = xavier_uniform(F, d, rng), np.zeros(d)

    p["lnf_g"], p["lnf_b"] = np.ones(d), np.zeros(d)
    p["head_w"], p["head_b"] = xavier_uniform(d, V, rng), np.zeros(V)

    return p

def attention_forward(Xn, params, p, cfg: ModelConfig):
    T, d = Xn.shape
    H = cfg.num_heads
    dh = d // H # width of one head

    Q = Xn @ params[p+"wq"] + params[p+"bq"]    # (T,d), QUERY
    K = Xn @ params[p+"wk"] + params[p+"bk"]    # KEY
    V = Xn @ params[p+"wv"] + params[p+"bv"]    # VALUE

    Qh, Kh, Vh = split_heads(Q, H), split_heads(K, H), split_heads(V, H)

    S = (Qh @ Kh.transpose(0, 2, 1)) / np.sqrt(dh)
    S = np.where(np.triu(np.ones((T, T), dtype=bool), 1), -np.inf, S)
    A = softmax_forward(S)
    O = merge_heads(A @ Vh)
    out = O @ params[p + "wo"] + params[p + "bo"]
    return out, dict(Xn=Xn, Qh=Qh, Kh=Kh, Vh=Vh, A=A, O=O)

leadingComments: receives the gradient on attention output and returns gradient on its input
given   dOut = ∂L/∂out         (T,d)   what arrives from the residual branch
fills   grads[p+"wo","bo","wq","bq","wk","bk","wv","bv"]
returns dXn  = ∂L/∂Xn          (T,d)   goes on to layer-norm 1's backward
functions.name: attention_backward
functions.signature: def attention_backward(dOut, c, params, p, cfg: ModelConfig, grads)
functions.source:
def attention_backward(dOut, c, params, p, cfg: ModelConfig, grads):
    H = cfg.num_heads
    dh = cfg.emb_dim // H
    grads[p + "wo"] += c["O"].T @ dOut
    grads[p + "bo"] += dOut.sum(axis=0)
    dOh = split_heads(dOut @ params[p + "wo"].T, H)
    dVh = c["A"].transpose(0, 2, 1) @ dOh 
    dA = dOh @ c["Vh"].transpose(0, 2, 1)
    dS = softmax_backward(c["A"], dA)
    dQh = dS @ c["Kh"] / np.sqrt(dh)
    dKh = dS.transpose(0, 2, 1) @ c["Qh"] / np.sqrt(dh)
    dQ, dK, dV = merge_heads(dQh), merge_heads(dKh), merge_heads(dVh)
    dXn = np.zeros_like(c["Xn"])
    for n, dM in (("q", dQ), ("k", dK), ("v", dV)):
        grads[p + "w" + n] += c["Xn"].T @ dM
        grads[p + "b" + n] += dM.sum(axis=0)
        dXn += dM @ params[p + "w" + n].T
    return dXn

def ffn_backward(dOut, c, params, p, grads):
    dA, dW2, db2 = linear_backward(c["A"], params[p + "ff2_w"], dOut)
    grads[p + "ff2_w"] += dW2
    grads[p + "ff2_b"] += db2
    dZ = relu_backward(c["Z"], dA)
    dXn, dW1, db1 = linear_backward(c["Xn"], params[p + "ff1_w"], dZ)

    grads[p + "ff1_w"] += dW1
    grads[p + "ff1_b"] += db1

    return dXn

def block_forward(X, params, l: int, cfg: ModelConfig):
    p = f"b{l}."
    Xn, c_ln1 = layer_norm_forward(X, params[p + "ln1_g"], params[p + "ln1_b"], cfg.ln_eps) # make a normalized copy for attention to read
    att, c_att = attention_forward(Xn, params, p, cfg) # each position gathers info from earlier positions
    X1 = X + att
    Xn2, c_ln2 = layer_norm_forward(X1, params[p + "ln2_g"], params[p + "ln2_b"], cfg.ln_eps) # normalized copy again, for the feed-forward
    ff, c_ff = ffn_forward(Xn2, params, p) # ach position thinks on its own

    return X1 + ff, dict(ln1=c_ln1, att=c_att, ln2=c_ln2, ff=c_ff)

functions.name: block_backward
functions.signature: def block_backward(dY, c, params, l, cfg: ModelConfig, grads)
functions.source:
def block_backward(dY, c, params, l, cfg: ModelConfig, grads):
    p = f"b{l}."
    dXn2 = ffn_backward(dY, c["ff"], params, p, grads)
    dX1_branch, dg, db = layer_norm_backward(dXn2, c["ln2"], params[p + "ln2_g"])
    grads[p + "ln2_g"] += dg
    grads[p + "ln2_b"] += db
    dX1 = dY + dX1_branch
    dXn = attention_backward(dX1, c["att"], params, p, cfg, grads)
    dX_branch, dg, db = layer_norm_backward(dXn, c["ln1"], params[p + "ln1_g"])
    grads[p + "ln1_g"] += dg
    grads[p + "ln1_b"] += db
    return dX1 + dX_branch

functions.name: loss_and_grads
functions.signature: def loss_and_grads(params, ids, targets, cfg: ModelConfig)
functions.source:
def loss_and_grads(params, ids, targets, cfg: ModelConfig):
    logits, cache = forward(params, ids, cfg)
    loss, probs = cross_entropy_forward(logits, targets)
    grads = {k: np.zeros_like(v) for k, v in params.items()}
    dZ = cross_entropy_backward(probs, targets)
    dXf, dW, db = linear_backward(cache["Xf"], params["head_w"], dZ)

    grads["head_w"] += dW
    grads["head_b"] += db

    dX, dg, db = layer_norm_backward(dXf, cache["lnf"], params["lnf_g"])

    grads["lnf_g"] += dg
    grads["lnf_b"] += db

    for l in reversed(range(cfg.num_layers)):
        dX = block_backward(dX, cache["blocks"][l], params, l, cfg, grads)
    embed_backward(dX, ids, grads)

    return loss, grads
